News Flash

Here's what you need to know to cast your ballot this election season

City News Posted on October 06, 2026

BANGOR, Maine – The election season is in full swing and here are some important points to keep in mind as Election Day nears. 

Early absentee voting has begun and can be done on the first floor of Bangor City Hall, 73 Harlow St. Early absentee voting at City Hall concludes on Thursday, Oct. 29, and ballots that are cast will be counted on election night, which is Tuesday, Nov. 3. 

Early voting also will be available at the Cross Insurance Center from Oct. 26 to 29, between the hours of 8 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. 

Absentee ballots are now available and the deadline to request such a ballot is Oct. 29. An absentee ballot can be obtained by calling the Bangor City Clerk & Treasury Office at 207-992-4220, or stopping by the office at City Hall. A written request for an absentee ballot also can be mailed to the office at City Hall, 73 Harlow St. And the Maine Secretary of State’s Office also provides them. 

Voter registration remains available to new voters and for existing Bangor voters to change their address or name. This can be done at the Cross Insurance Center on Election Day; at the CIC during early voting from Oct. 26 to 29; and at City Hall during regular business hours, 8 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Registration also can be done online at the Secretary of State’s Office. 

All voting on Election Day – Tuesday, Nov. 3 – will be done at the Cross Insurance Center, 515 Main St. in Bangor. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. 

And don’t forget that the Community Connector will offer free rides to anyone wishing to vote on Election Day. For other voting- and election-related information, please visit this page at bangormaine.gov.

###

The City of Bangor, Maine, is a service center community of 31,753 residents and is the county seat of Penobscot County. Bangor is the major commercial and cultural center for much of northern and eastern Maine. The City is an equal opportunity employer and service provider. For information on City projects and news, see www.bangormaine.gov
